title: Finite projective syntomic conormal and its fibre dimension rank
statement: Call a map $T\to E$ syntomic if it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and every fibre $E\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $R\to S$ be syntomic and let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow S$ be an $R$-algebra presentation with finitely generated kernel $J$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $J/J^2$ is a finite projective $S$-module, meaning a direct summand of a finite free $S$-module. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $F=S\otimes_R k$ and $\bar J=\ker(k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to F)$. The canonical map $(J/J^2)\otimes_S F\to\bar J/\bar J^2$, induced by coefficient reduction, is an isomorphism. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset F$, the localization $(\bar J/\bar J^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $n-\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}F)$, where dimension at a point means the local topological dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], not the Krull dimension of the local ring $F_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 07BT (lemma-syntomic-presentation-ideal-mod-squares), g=1; Tag 00SC (lemma-lci), (1) implies (4). The fibre comparison follows by tensoring 0 -> J -> P -> S -> 0, using R-flatness of S; this uses flatness of the quotient, not flatness of R -> k.

proof.text: Put $N=J/J^2$. Fix a prime $q$ of $S$ and put $p=q\cap R$. The local map $R_p\to S_q$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]. In the fibre $F_p=S\otimes_R\kappa(p)$ the kernel $Q$ of $F_p\to\kappa(q)$ is a prime: the map sends $s\otimes a$ to $\bar s a$ and has domain a nonzero ring because it maps unitally to the field $\kappa(q)$. The local-complete-intersection hypothesis, unpacked using [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], gives $h\notin Q$ with $(F_p)_h$ a global complete intersection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection] with finite-presentation neighbourhood $g=1$, this local flatness and this $h$. It gives $g_q\in S\setminus q$ and a presentation $S_{g_q}\cong R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/H$ which is a relative global complete intersection, with $H=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$.

source.place: Tag 07BT (lemma-syntomic-presentation-ideal-mod-squares), first sentence of proof; Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic), (3) implies (2).

proof.text: For the chart $g=g_q$ of step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-module-principal-localization] applied to the given presentation of $S$ and the chosen presentation of $S_g$ gives $N_g\oplus S_g^m\cong(H/H^2)\oplus S_g^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal-free], the right side is $S_g^{c+n}$. Thus $N_g$ is a direct summand of a finite free module: inclusion and projection of its first summand, conjugated by the displayed isomorphism, exhibit the splitting. In particular it is finitely generated and projective over $S_g$.

source.place: Tag 07BT, last sentence of proof, using Tags 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize) and 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal).

proof.text: The prime $q$ determines a prime of $S_{g_q}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] to the finite projective module $N_{g_q}$ of step 2 at that prime. Obtain an element $h=a/g_q^r$ outside it such that $(N_{g_q})_h$ is finite free over $(S_{g_q})_h$. Here $a\notin q$. Inverting $g_q$ and $a/g_q^r$ is the same as inverting $g_q a$: both rings have precisely the universal property of making $g_q$ and $a$ units. The corresponding module fractions identify $(N_{g_q})_h=N_{g_q a}$. Consequently every prime $q$ has a standard neighbourhood $D(t_q)$, $t_q=g_q a\notin q$, on which $N$ is finite free.

source.place: Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), (3) implies (7), refining the cover in the proof of Tag 07BT.

proof.text: The $D(t_q)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] their elements generate the unit ideal. An expression of $1$ as a finite sum of multiples of these elements selects finitely many $t_1,\ldots,t_l$ generating that ideal. Each $N_{t_i}$ is finite free by step 3, so [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective] gives that $N$ is finite projective over $S$, i.e. finitely generated and projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. This is the direct-summand sense of the statement: finitely many generators $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ of $N$ give a surjection $\pi:S^{\oplus r}\to N$, $e_i\mapsto n_i$, and the lifting property of the projective module $N$ in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] lifts $\mathrm{id}_N$ along $\pi$ to $\sigma:N\to S^{\oplus r}$ with $\pi\sigma=\mathrm{id}_N$, so $N$ is a direct summand of $S^{\oplus r}$. This argument includes $S=0$: the empty family generates its unit ideal and $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 07BT, reduction using Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective); Tags 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology) and 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact) for the finite standard cover.

proof.text: Fix now an arbitrary prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ and set $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $F=S\otimes_R k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to J\to P\to S\to0$ over $R$, with flat quotient $S$ and tensor factor $k$. It gives $0\to k\otimes_R J\to k\otimes_R P\to k\otimes_R S\to0$. Under the polynomial scalar-extension isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], the middle term is $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and the last arrow is the given coefficient-reduced presentation of $F$. Therefore the injection identifies $k\otimes_R J$ with its kernel $\bar J$. The identification sends $a\otimes j$ to $a\bar j$; in particular $\bar J$ is generated by the reductions of elements of $J$. No flatness of $k$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); coefficient-reduced presentation as in the proof of Tag 00SY (lemma-syntomic).

proof.text: Tensor $J^2\to J\to N\to0$ with $k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Under step 5, the image of $k\otimes_R J^2$ in $\bar J$ is exactly $\bar J^2$: a term $a\otimes jj'$ maps to $a\bar j\bar j'$, and conversely a product of sums of terms $a\bar j$ expands into such terms; coefficients from $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ can be absorbed in $j$ because $J$ is an ideal. Thus $k\otimes_R N\cong\bar J/\bar J^2$, sending $a\otimes[j]$ to $a[\bar j]$. Finally $N\otimes_S F\cong k\otimes_R N$ explicitly by $[j]\otimes(s\otimes a)\mapsto a\otimes s[j]$, with inverse $a\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes a)$. The balancing relations show these are inverse. Their composite is precisely the coefficient-reduction map asserted in the statement, hence proves that this canonical map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), applied to J^2 -> J -> J/J^2 -> 0, after the flat-quotient injection of Tag 00HL.

proof.text: For any prime $\mathfrak q$ of $F$, the hypothesis that $F$ is a local complete intersection, unpacked using [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], supplies $u\in F\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $F_u$ a global complete intersection over $k$. The polynomial presentation of step 5 identifies $F$ with $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/\bar J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] to this presentation, $\mathfrak q$ and $u$. It says that $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}F)$ is an integer between $0$ and $n$ and that $(\bar J/\bar J^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $n-d$. Its dimension is explicitly the topological dimension at the point, as required. If $F=0$ there is no such prime, while the isomorphism in step 6 is still the zero-module isomorphism. This proves every remaining clause.

lean.statement: theorem syntomic_presentation_conormal_fibre_rank {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S] [FinitePresentation R S] (hci : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, IsLocalCompleteIntersection p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber S)) (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] S) (hα : Function.Surjective α) (hJ : (RingHom.ker α.toRingHom).FG) : (∃ (m : ℕ) (i : (Extension.ofSurjective α hα).Cotangent →ₗ[S] (Fin m → S)) (r : (Fin m → S) →ₗ[S] (Extension.ofSurjective α hα).Cotangent), r.comp i = LinearMap.id) ∧ ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, (∃ e : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] (Extension.ofSurjective α hα).Cotangent ≃ₗ[p.asIdeal.ResidueField] ((Generators.ofAlgHom α hα).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).toExtension.Cotangent, ∀ (a : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) (j : (Extension.ofSurjective α hα).ker) (j' : ((Generators.ofAlgHom α hα).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).toExtension.ker), j'.val = MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) j.val → e (a ⊗ₜ[R] Extension.Cotangent.mk j) = a • Extension.Cotangent.mk j') ∧ ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (p.asIdeal.Fiber S), ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDimAt q = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ d ≤ n ∧ Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin (n - d)) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl ((Generators.ofAlgHom α hα).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).toExtension.Cotangent))
